headline: GitHub Enterprise now includes Copilot for every licensed user, with AI usage billed against your budget from the first request
tldr: GitHub's pricing page now lists "GitHub Copilot access" in the Enterprise plan. There are no per-seat AI credits: Chat, code review and cloud agents draw on the company's AI budget.
actions: If your company is on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with an account team, ask them about moving to the Copilot-included model, and compare it with what you pay now for Copilot Business or Enterprise seats
Set an enterprise AI budget, policies and alerts before you switch, since usage is metered from the first request with no included allowance
If you manage your own Enterprise subscription, nothing changes yet. GitHub says self-serve access opens in stages, with dates to come

redline.after: AI-powered development, governed at enterprise scale
redline.label: Pricing · Enterprise plan tagline
redline.note: The Enterprise plan is now pitched as an AI plan first.

redline.after: GitHub Enterprise now includes access to GitHub Copilot. Learn more Everything from Team, plus: GitHub Copilot access Agent governance
redline.label: Pricing · Enterprise features
redline.note: Copilot access and "Agent governance" are now listed as Enterprise features.

what:
GitHub redesigned its pricing page around Copilot. The page's banner changed from "Try GitHub, the complete developer platform" to "Try the Copilot-powered platform", and the Enterprise plan's tagline went from "Security, compliance, and flexible deployment" to "AI-powered development, governed at enterprise scale". The Enterprise box now opens with "GitHub Enterprise now includes access to GitHub Copilot." and its feature list starts with "GitHub Copilot access" and "Agent governance". Its comparison table lists Enterprise at $21 per user/month.

Change 1: Copilot comes with Enterprise, but with no AI credits. GitHub's changelog post from October 28, 2026 says enterprises "working with a GitHub or Microsoft account team can now get Copilot included with GitHub Enterprise for every licensed user." It has "the same features and models as Copilot Enterprise but does not include monthly AI credits per seat." Instead, "AI usage is metered from the first request against your enterprise budget" and "There is no included usage allowance to track or top up."

Change 2: what works when the budget runs out. Per the changelog, "Code completion and next edit suggestions keep working even with no budget available," while "Copilot Chat, Copilot code review, and Copilot in the cloud require available budget to use." It adds: "An exhausted budget never removes access."

Change 3: people without an Enterprise license. Users in an enterprise account who don't hold a GitHub Enterprise license "get the same Copilot access through Copilot Standalone, at $10 per user per month."

Who can get it now: only customers on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with an account team. For self-serve customers it is "Currently unavailable", and GitHub says it will open it "in stages and will share dates in the coming weeks." Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise "remain available to purchase."

Other changes: the Team and Enterprise price boxes no longer carry the line "for the first 12 months". The Free and Team plans keep the same CI/CD minutes (2,000 and 3,000 a month) and Packages storage (500MB and 2GB).
who: Companies on GitHub Enterprise Cloud, and the developers and finance teams who manage their Copilot spend. Individuals and teams on Free or Team aren't affected, and self-serve Enterprise customers can't switch yet.
seo_title: GitHub Enterprise now includes Copilot (Oct 28, 2026): no AI credits, usage billed to your budget
seo_desc: GitHub's pricing page now lists Copilot access in Enterprise. Per GitHub, it has no per-seat AI credits: usage is metered against the enterprise budget, and Chat, code review and cloud agents need budget. Copilot Standalone is $10/user/month.
faq: Does GitHub Enterprise include Copilot now?

Yes, for Enterprise Cloud customers working with a GitHub or Microsoft account team. GitHub's pricing page says "GitHub Enterprise now includes access to GitHub Copilot." Self-serve customers can't get it yet.
Does Copilot in GitHub Enterprise include AI credits?
No. GitHub's changelog says it "does not include monthly AI credits per seat" and that "AI usage is metered from the first request against your enterprise budget."
What happens when the AI budget runs out?
Code completion and next edit suggestions keep working. Copilot Chat, Copilot code review and Copilot in the cloud need available budget. GitHub says "An exhausted budget never removes access."
sources: GitHub Changelog: GitHub Enterprise now includes access to GitHub Copilot (Oct 28, 2026)

headline: Social Security is building one 'Client Data System' profile on everyone with an SSN, combining 12 record systems
tldr: A new SSA records system keeps one profile per SSN: citizenship, earnings, benefits, marriage history, call notes, alert flags. Email may be used for surveys. Comments close Nov 29.
actions: Comment by Nov 29, 2026 at regulations.gov, docket SSA-2025-0030 (or by mail to SSA's Head of Privacy and Disclosure Policy, Room G-401 West High Rise, 6401 Security Blvd, Baltimore, MD 21235-6401)
Check the contact and text-message preferences in your my Social Security account, since the new system tracks opt-ins and can use your email for outreach and surveys
To see your record, send SSA a written request with your name and SSN plus a notarized statement or signed identity certification (contact LP.PDP.SORN@ssa.gov)

redline.before: This system maintains information about individuals who visit an SSA office, including those conducting business with SSA
redline.after: This system maintains information on individuals who have been issued a Social Security number (SSN), including those who have conducted business with SSA beyond enumeration.
redline.label: Who's covered · Customer Service Record System (60-0350) vs. new Client Data System (60-0392)
redline.note: Office visitors before; anyone ever issued an SSN now, in one profile retrieved by SSN.

redline.after: We may also use contact information (e.g., email addresses) provided by individuals who conduct business with SSA for program outreach (e.g., notification about our programs, online services, SSA events, and surveys)
redline.label: Client Data System · Purposes
redline.note: A new stated use for the email address you give SSA.

redline.after: customer interaction history, including notes or remarks entered by technicians; and details of customer contact and verification history
redline.label: Client Data System · Categories of records
redline.note: Call and office notes sit in the same profile as earnings, benefits, citizenship and marriage data.

what: The Social Security Administration (SSA) is creating a new Privacy Act system of records called the Client Data System (60-0392). The notice is on public inspection now and is scheduled to be published in the Federal Register on October 30, 2026 (FR Doc. 2026-22173, docket SSA-2025-0030). SSA says it will "track and manage information about a customer including personal information and customer interactions" and give employees "one main location to view information concerning the customer." The notice lists no history (it is a new system) and claims no Privacy Act exemptions. Change 1: one profile for everyone with an SSN. The notice says the system "maintains information on individuals who have been issued a Social Security number (SSN), including those who have conducted business with SSA beyond enumeration." Records are retrieved "by the number holder's SSN." That covers anyone who has ever been issued a number, not only people who receive benefits. For comparison, SSA's existing customer-service records system (Appointments, Visitor Information, and Customer Service Record System, 60-0350, republished August 20, 2025) covers "individuals who visit an SSA office" or make an appointment. Change 2: what goes into it. The new system pulls data "primarily from existing SSA systems of records," and the notice names 12 of them, including the Master Files of SSN Holders (60-0058), the Earnings Recording system (60-0059), Claims Folders (60-0089), the Master Beneficiary Record (60-0090), the SSI record (60-0103), the Medicare Database File (60-0321), the Digital Identity File System (60-0373) and the Customer Engagement Tools system (60-0383). It also takes data from "third parties such as a contractor or vendor; and Federal, State, and local agencies." The record categories in one place include: name, SSN, sex, date of birth, parent names and place of birth; "country of citizenship"; mailing and email address, phone, language and texting opt-ins; "customer interaction history, including notes or remarks entered by technicians"; representative payee and appointed representative details, including fee agreements; benefit and SSI payment amounts; "yearly earnings and quarters of coverage"; accommodation needs such as Braille, interpreters or hearing loops; marriage details including the spouse's SSN, "reason for marriage end" and "marriage type"; "electronic block, high-risk, and special indicator warnings"; and indicators for the Defense Department's Wounded Warrior program and a VA "100% Permanent and Total Disability Compensation Rating." Change 3: a new use for your email address. The notice adds: "We may also use contact information (e.g., email addresses) provided by individuals who conduct business with SSA for program outreach (e.g., notification about our programs, online services, SSA events, and surveys) and other purposes related to our administration of the Social Security Act." We did not find that outreach wording in the source notices we checked (60-0350, 60-0383 and 60-0058). Other listed purposes include tracking "consent to text," identity verification, "prevention of fraud," research, staffing decisions and "agency strategic goals and funding decisions." Change 4: who it can be shared with. The notice lists 30 routine uses, which take effect 30 days after publication. Most match uses already in SSA's other notices. They include the Department of Homeland Security "upon request, to identify and locate aliens in the United States" under 8 U.S.C. 1360(b) (SSA's Master Files notice, 60-0058, already has this use); "Federal, State, and local law enforcement agencies and private security contractors" for office safety and related investigations; law enforcement investigating criminal violations of the Social Security Act; "private collection under contract with us" to recover overpayments; Treasury's Do Not Pay system; state agencies running Medicaid, TANF and food stamps (SNAP); contractors, other agencies and researchers under written agreements; and employers and private pension plans in situations where a person's whereabouts are unknown. SSA says it will not disclose IRS "return or return information" unless authorized. What stays the same: SSA says the data comes mainly from systems it already keeps, so the notice doesn't describe new information being collected from you. What changes is that it all sits in one SSN-indexed profile, along with interaction notes and alert flags that until now were kept in separate systems. You can't opt out of a system of records. You can ask for your record or contest it, but the notice says you "may need to identify each system of records in which the individual seeks to correct or amend the record" and follow each one's procedure. Coverage (checked October 29): we found nothing in news searches or on X about the Client Data System notice, which goes on public inspection on October 29. SSA's sharing of data with DHS under its Master Files notice was widely reported in 2025. This notice is separate. What you can do: comment by November 29, 2026 (30 days after publication) at regulations.gov under docket SSA-2025-0030, or by mail to the Head of Privacy and Disclosure Policy, Law and Policy, SSA, Room G-401 West High Rise, 6401 Security Boulevard, Baltimore, MD 21235-6401. Questions go to LP.PDP.SORN@ssa.gov or (410) 965-1727. If you'd rather not get outreach email or texts, check the contact and messaging preferences in your my Social Security account. To see what SSA holds on you, send a written request with your name and SSN to the system manager, with a notarized statement or a signed certification of identity.
who: Anyone who has been issued a Social Security number, including people who have never claimed benefits. Retirees, SSI recipients, people with representative payees or appointed representatives, and anyone who has contacted SSA have the most data in it.
seo_title: SSA Client Data System (60-0392): new Social Security profile on every SSN holder, comments due Nov 29, 2026
seo_desc: Social Security's new Client Data System (SORN 60-0392, Oct 30, 2026) combines 12 record systems into one profile per SSN: citizenship, earnings, benefits, marriage, call notes and alert flags. Email used for outreach. Who can get it and how to comment.
faq: What is the SSA Client Data System?

A new Social Security Administration system of records (60-0392), announced in a Privacy Act notice scheduled for the October 30, 2026 Federal Register (FR Doc. 2026-22173). It gives SSA employees "one main location to view information concerning the customer," built mainly from 12 existing SSA record systems.
The notice says it covers "individuals who have been issued a Social Security number (SSN), including those who have conducted business with SSA beyond enumeration." Records are retrieved by SSN.

Identity data (name, SSN, sex, date of birth, parents' names, place of birth), country of citizenship, contact details and texting opt-ins, interaction history including technicians' notes, representative payee and appointed representative details, benefit and SSI payment amounts, yearly earnings, accommodation needs, marriage details including the spouse's SSN and why a marriage ended, high-risk and other alert flags, and Wounded Warrior and VA 100% disability indicators.
Can SSA share it with DHS or law enforcement?

Yes, under its routine uses. The list includes DHS "upon request, to identify and locate aliens in the United States" under 8 U.S.C. 1360(b), a use SSA's Master Files notice (60-0058) already includes, plus law enforcement and private security contractors for office safety, criminal investigations of Social Security Act violations, private collection contractors for overpayments, Treasury's Do Not Pay system and state benefit agencies. The routine uses take effect 30 days after publication.

It may. The notice says SSA may use email addresses and other contact information "for program outreach (e.g., notification about our programs, online services, SSA events, and surveys)." The system also tracks texting opt-ins and opt-outs.
Can I opt out or comment?

You can't opt out of a system of records. You can comment until November 29, 2026 at regulations.gov (docket SSA-2025-0030) or by mail, and you can ask SSA for your record or contest it under its Privacy Act rules.
